findings.reason: §4 should invoke `imas map run FACILITY` once and let §8's landed target selection iterate, instead of forking per-IDS enumeration into sequence.py.
findings.text: the `mapping` stage re-derives the facility's IDS targets itself ("run imas map run for each IDS that holds a selected or escalated candidate edge … read through the candidate reader") when `imas map run FACILITY` already enumerates targets through `discover_mappable_ids` (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:376, called at imas_codex/cli/map.py:211) and mapping-candidate-selection §8 has `imas map run` itself consume the candidate edges (selected/escalated/no_candidate); a second target-selection path will drift from that owner

findings.reason: §2 should extend `ServiceMonitor`'s checks (or reuse `ssh_health_check`/`wiki_auth_check` rather than a fresh probe set) and derive the registry's domain list from `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS`, so one owner holds facility access and one holds the domain set.
findings.text: the plan builds a new access-probe orchestration over `check_ssh_connection`/`probe_remote_environment` and a new domain enumeration alongside two existing owners: (a) the facility-access probe owner `create_service_monitor` (imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py:1117) / `ServiceMonitor` (imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py:830), with `neo4j_health_check` (imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py:159), `ssh_health_check` (imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py:178) and `wiki_auth_check` (imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py:200), reached by every discover command through `create_discovery_monitor` (imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:502); and (b) `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` (imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:30), the existing ordered domain enumeration that `domain_option` (imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:427) already validates against

findings.reason: the registry should name each stage's predicate as its existing `has_pending_*` owner (or add one where none exists) rather than implying a new predicate per stage, which is a census that decides where the skip reason comes from.
findings.text: §2 says each stage records "the predicate that says whether it has work" without citing any owner, but those pending-work predicates already exist per domain and are the only thing that can make "skipped: nothing to do" true or false: imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:198 `has_pending_work`; imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:549 `has_pending_work`, :556 `has_pending_enrich_work`, :587 `has_pending_check_work`; imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:579 `has_pending_scan_work`, :627 `has_pending_score_work`, :655 `has_pending_triage_work`, :682 `has_pending_enrich_work`, :717 `has_pending_code_work`; imas_codex/ids/workers.py:386 `has_pending_mapping_work`, :395 `has_pending_validation_work`, :404 `has_pending_candidate_work`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one module (`sequence.py`) holds the ordered registry, the run loop, the probe delegation and the report table behind a single small surface, rather than spreading the same behaviour over many wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements two shared mechanisms: IDS-target selection (§4 re-derives which IDS hold candidates beside `discover_mappable_ids`) and facility-access probing (§2 builds a parallel probe orchestration beside the `ServiceMonitor` every discover command already uses).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 names the one CLI entry it adds and, in its own text, states that it retires none and why the per-domain commands must stay (they carry stage-specific options), which is the "why nothing can be" account the item requires.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites some prior art (`run_discovery`, `check_ssh_connection`, `probe_remote_environment`, `verify_tunnel`/`is_tunnel_active`) but omits the existing access-probe owner `ServiceMonitor`/`create_service_monitor` and every existing pending-work predicate (`has_pending_*`), which §2's "skipped: nothing to do" outcome must rest on.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the runner is a thin loop over the existing click commands, and §3 states the justification the item asks for: `ctx.invoke` is the only path that reuses each stage whole "without refactoring seven commands or starting subprocesses".
